text.arabic_uthmani: وَقَدْ مَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرَهُمْ وَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَكْرُهُمْ وَإِن كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ

words.gloss_range: opening conjunction linking the disclosed plotting to the prior warning scene
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens by attaching the ayah to the prior warning, so the report of plotting arrives as disclosed continuation rather than a detached notice. It links backward, delays the human actor until the verb, and lets the completed deception explain the scene already shown.

topics.headline: linked disclosure frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plotting is presented as the disclosed state behind the preceding warning, not as a new isolated report.
topics.reason: The opening conjunction is licensed as narrative/circumstantial linkage before the completed plotting clause.

topics.headline: boundary link before actor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that continuity is heard before any schemer is named, making the ayah belong to the prior argument first.
topics.reason: The boundary rows show the particle carrying the prior addressed scene into third-person forensic narration.

words.gloss_range: certainty particle verifying the completed past plotting before the divine counter-presence is stated
words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) certifies the following perfect verb as completed action. Before the ayah turns to divine custody, the particle makes the plot a verified past fact, and with the opening connector it packages continuity and completion together.

topics.headline: verified completed plotting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plot is not merely narrated in the past; it is certified as already complete before God's holding of it is named.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a certainty particle before a perfect verb, selecting completion rather than probability.

topics.headline: continuity plus verification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first two words fuse carry-over from the prior ayah with verification of the hidden mechanism behind it.
topics.reason: The source rows connect the particle cluster to the transition from prior disclosure to established backstory.

words.gloss_range: completed human plotting, intensified by the following cognate accusative and repeated root field
words.root_gloss_range: root range of scheming, strategic twisting, and counter-strategy; local use is human plotting under completed perfect aspect
words.prose: {{ar:مَكَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:makarū}}) is the completed human act, but it does not take a normal external object; the following cognate maṣdar intensifies the act as their very scheme. The m-k-r field keeps a twisting, strategic pressure, locally negative because the carried-over actors are wrongdoers, while the Form I perfect keeps the action direct before the syntax relocates the plot to God. That first human makr also starts the ayah's fourfold reprise and belongs to the wider divine-counterstrategy field seen at 3:54 and 8:30, while the local boundary narrows the prior self-wronging scene into the operative technique behind 14:45, with 14:22 as nearby failed-scheming pressure.

topics.headline: completed act intensified by cognate noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb and following maṣdar make the plotting a completed, intensified, nameable act rather than a casual past action.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect under qad, and the following same-root maṣdar is constrained as cognate accusative rather than a normal object.

topics.headline: twisted strategy judged by local agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root's strategic twisting image while also seeing that its moral charge comes from the local wrongdoer frame.
topics.reason: Root evidence supports strategic/twisting range, while the preceding wrongdoer context narrows the local valuation negatively.

topics.headline: direct finite human action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah charges a finished action by the schemers, not a causative stem or a mere agent label.
topics.reason: The surface is Form I perfect with 3mp agreement, so broader causative or participial branches do not control the local parse.

topics.headline: recurring makr field under local syntax
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human makr begins a fourfold local reprise and belongs to a wider divine-counterstrategy field, including concrete makr parallels at 3:54 and 8:30.
topics.reason: The parallels and recurrence are retained as interpretive pressure, but local syntax still governs this first verb as human completed action.

topics.headline: wrongdoing becomes concrete technique
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah narrows the prior self-wronging scene into the operative technique of scheming, with nearby surah pressure from 14:22 and 14:45.
topics.reason: The boundary rows link the verb to the preceding moral category and to local sound/repetition without replacing the grammatical reading.

words.gloss_range: owned maṣdar of plotting functioning as cognate accusative, turning the action into a possessed product
words.root_gloss_range: same scheming root as word 3, here nominalized as an owned process/product in cognate accusative position
words.prose: {{ar:مَكْرَهُمْ}} ({{tr:makrahum}}) turns the action into their owned maṣdar, with the suffix carrying the prior wrongdoer class into the noun without renaming them. As cognate accusative it amplifies the verb, but as a possessed process-and-product noun it also prepares the later role change: the same scheme will move from object of their act to subject located with God.

topics.headline: owned cognate object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the scheme is both intensified by same-root grammar and grammatically owned by the actors.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as cognate accusative, and the suffix makes the maṣdar definite and possessed.

topics.headline: same group as owners
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the possessive suffix carries the prior wrongdoer class into the plot noun without renaming them.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence supports the suffix route back to the inherited third-person group.

topics.headline: act becomes twisted product
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the maṣdar is both the plotting process and the plotted product, making relocation to God possible later.
topics.reason: The nominal form objectifies the action while the same-root pair keeps the intensifying process sense active.

topics.headline: first step in role reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first case role in a sequence: accusative product here, nominative subject with God next.
topics.reason: The rows track the same gerund through repeated syntactic roles, a major structural payoff of the ayah.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial or parenthetical conjunction inserting the divine-location clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does more than add another event. It opens a circumstantial or parenthetical nominal clause, inserting God's custody of the plot between human action and the later mountain-scale condition; this is the second of three differently functioning connectors.

topics.headline: divine holding inserted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine custody interrupts the movement from human plotting to the scale test, preventing a simple action chain.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following nominal clause as coordinated/circumstantial, not a new human event.

topics.headline: three connector functions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same connector sound segments the ayah into narrative, circumstantial, and concessive beats.
topics.reason: The row family compares all three connectors and is locally coherent with the clause segmentation.

words.gloss_range: fronted locative/custodial predicate: the plot is with, known by, and under God
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes nearness, possession, presence, and the adjacent family of obstinate resistance; local use is locative/custodial predicate
words.prose: {{ar:عِندَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}) is the fronted locative predicate: the reader reaches God's domain before the plot is named again. Its range is not merely spatial; proximity, possession, knowledge, and custody converge, with an ironic same-surah pressure from obstinate resistance at 14:15 and divine nearness language at 14:37. Even the dominant ʿinda-plus-Allāh relation is made specific by what is held here: their plot.

topics.headline: fronted divine domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that location is the first claim of the nominal clause: God's domain frames the plot before the plot reappears.
topics.reason: The word is an accusative ẓarf in construct and functions as fronted predicate before the delayed subject.

topics.headline: with, held, and known
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plot is at once near, held, known, and controlled, not merely observed from a distance.
topics.reason: The semantic range of ʿinda supports spatial, custodial, and epistemic values that reinforce the local predicate.

topics.headline: nearness answers obstinacy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that the resistant ʿ-n-d field is answered by a phrase of nearness and custody at God, with concrete same-surah pressure at 14:15 and 14:37.
topics.reason: The root-family echo survives as contextual pressure, while the local surface remains the locative ʿinda rather than an adjective of obstinacy.

topics.headline: common formula made local
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a dominant ʿinda-plus-Allāh relation is made specific by what is held here: their plot.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence and sound rows are retained as local support, though they do not add a separate grammar claim.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name completing the locative construct as the named domain of custody
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name; derivational and refuge/bewilderment pressures are contextual, while local grammar makes the name the genitive domain after ʿinda

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the preceding locative construct head governing the divine name

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) completes the construct after {{ar:عِندَ}} ({{tr:ʿinda}}), making the named God the domain in which the plot is held. The proper name prevents a generic divine-realm reading and sits structurally between repeated makr forms, so the plot cannot continue its chain without passing through the divine name. Refuge, worship, and bewilderment pressures remain around the name, while the local grammar keeps it a proper genitive domain; the same-surah question about God at 14:10 is answered here by the scheme standing with God.

topics.headline: named divine domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plot is located with the named God specifically, not with an abstract divine category.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the proper noun as genitive complement of the locative construct.

topics.headline: proper name, not generic deity noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that refuge, worship, and bewilderment pressures surround the name, while the local parse remains the proper divine name in construct.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute is retained as semantic pressure but narrowed by the surface proper-name function.

topics.headline: divine name interrupts makr chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a very common divine name becomes locally marked because it stands at the structural center against a dense cluster of scheming language.
topics.reason: The rows support the divine name as the pivot between human scheme and the repeated God-held scheme.

topics.headline: same-surah divine-name contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a same-surah contrast: the question about God at 14:10 is answered here by the scheme standing with God.
topics.reason: The concrete reference is retained as contextual echo, not as a change in local grammar.

words.gloss_range: possessed plot as delayed nominative subject after the divine-location predicate
words.root_gloss_range: same scheming root, now a nominative possessed maṣdar as delayed subject in the divine-location clause
words.prose: {{ar:مَكْرُهُمْ}} ({{tr:makruhum}}) repeats the owned plot, but now as delayed nominative subject after the divine-location predicate. The same human suffix remains, so ownership is not erased; it is inverted, because their scheme is introduced only after God's custody has already framed it. The repetition is forensic rather than decorative: the same scheme returns under a new grammatical angle.

topics.headline: accusative plot becomes nominative subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a small case shift changes the same plot from object of human action into subject located with God.
topics.reason: The noun is nominative delayed subject after a fronted predicate, reversing the earlier accusative role.

topics.headline: owned by humans, held by God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human possession and divine custody overlap in one clause rather than cancelling each other.
topics.reason: The suffix preserves human ownership while the fronted predicate places the same owned thing in God's domain.

topics.headline: second gerund in forensic chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repetition is forensic: the same scheme is brought back under a new grammatical angle, not merely repeated for sound.
topics.reason: The rows connect the repeated gerund to the boundary movement from visible evidence to divine record.

words.gloss_range: concessive conjunction opening the final even-if scale-test

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the following conditional particle that forms the concessive cluster

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) begins the final turn as concession. Joined to {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}), it opens an even-if frame after the divine-location clause, so the mountain image is processed under God's custody rather than as an independent claim about the plot.

topics.headline: even-if pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final scale test is subordinate to what has just been said about divine custody.
topics.reason: QAC marks concessive function, and the clause evidence links the conditional to the preceding nominal assertion.

topics.headline: third connector completes sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's connector architecture completing: opening link, middle insertion, final concession.
topics.reason: The row coheres with the three-wāw segmentation already visible across the ayah.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle with live concessive, negative, and variant-driven polarity pressure
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) is the pressure point of the final clause. As conditional it sets an extreme even-if hypothesis; through negative and variant evidence it can also diminish the plot by denying mountain-moving capacity, so the scale of the plot changes at this particle before the mountains are named. The kāda variant makes the same area a near-miss reading, where the plot almost moves mountains rather than simply being conceded or denied.

topics.headline: extreme conditional frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mountain movement is framed as a condition or concession, with the answer compressed under the prior divine-custody claim.
topics.reason: The particle governs the kāna clause as conditional protasis, so the following image is not a simple assertion.

topics.headline: conditional or negating reparse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same surface can generate opposed scale readings: terrifying concession or denial of capacity.
topics.reason: The negative reading and wa-mā variant are retained as serious apparatus, while the canonical local parse remains conditional unless that reading is selected.

topics.headline: near-occurrence variant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a variant can recast the plot as almost moving mountains, which confirms that this particle area controls the scale reading.
topics.reason: The kāda variant is apparatus for the interpretive pressure point and does not override the local kāna surface.

words.gloss_range: incomplete copula placing the plot in a hypothetical state measured by the following lām-clause
words.root_gloss_range: being/state root; local use is the incomplete copula inside a conditional frame, not a causative creation stem
words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) is an incomplete copula inside the conditional frame: the subject is the possessed plot, and the predicate content is supplied by the lām-governed mountain-departure clause. It tests the plot as a state or capacity in the register of being, not as a creator of reality, with variant pressure from a near-occurrence reading and same-surah z-w-l pressure from 14:44.

topics.headline: plot as subject, departure as predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final beat is built as a conditional copular test, not a direct action statement by the schemers.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies makruhum as subject of kāna and the lām-clause as predicate content under conditional scope.

topics.headline: scheme tested as state of being
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the scheme is examined as a state or capacity in the register of being before it is measured against mountain departure.
topics.reason: The k-w-n semantic range supports state/being pressure, and local syntax applies it to the plot.

topics.headline: not causative creation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the limit: broader creation or near-occurrence possibilities sharpen the reading, but the surface is the basic copula; same-surah z-w-l pressure includes 14:44.
topics.reason: The causative derivative is not the local form, and the kāda reading is variant apparatus rather than the standard surface.

words.gloss_range: third possessed plot noun, now the subject of kāna and candidate force under evaluation
words.root_gloss_range: same possessed scheming maṣdar, now the subject of kāna inside the final scale-test
words.prose: {{ar:مَكْرُهُمْ}} ({{tr:makruhum}}) returns the same possessed plot for the final test. As ism kāna, it is no longer merely the product they performed or the subject held with God; it becomes the candidate force whose possible relation to mountain departure is being evaluated. This completes the forensic chain from object to delayed subject to ism kāna, while a variant can reparse the same plot as the source phrase rather than the nominative subject.

topics.headline: owned plot as subject of kāna
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same owned scheme persists into the final condition instead of becoming plotting in general.
topics.reason: The word is nominative as ism kāna, and the suffix continues the prior group.

topics.headline: plot measured against mountains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the tactile contrast: a twisted human strategy is tested as a possible cause against the fixity of mountains.
topics.reason: The maṣdar subject is linked to the following mountain-departure predicate, making the same scheme the object of escalating scrutiny.

topics.headline: third forensic reprise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the third gerund completes a chain of grammatical re-examination: object, delayed subject, then subject of kāna.
topics.reason: The rows identify the repeated m-k-r sequence as a structural chain rather than redundant repetition.

topics.headline: variant makes plot source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a variant can recast the plot from nominative subject into source phrase, confirming that the final clause pivots on the plot's grammatical role.
topics.reason: The lawlā variant is retained as apparatus but does not replace the local ism-kāna parse.

words.gloss_range: governing lām that makes the mountain-departure verb dependent as purpose, result, or denied capacity
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) is the small governor that controls the final verb. It can route the mountain departure as purpose, result, or, under a negative reading of the previous particle, denied capacity; in every case the verb remains dependent rather than independent. Because the proclitic is fused to the verb, the hinge from plot-state to mountain departure is visible in the written form itself.

topics.headline: purpose, result, or denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final image changes depending on this lām: intended goal, consequence, or impossibility.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the lām as governing the subjunctive verb in a purpose/result predicate, with denial possible under the negative parse.

topics.headline: governor fused to verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the graphic fusion of particle and verb makes dependency visible at the hinge from plot-state to mountain departure.
topics.reason: The proclitic attaches directly to tazūla and marks the transition into the final predicate image.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive intransitive departure of the mountains from fixed position, with variant mood pressure
words.root_gloss_range: root range of departing, ceasing, shifting from place, and decline; local Form I intransitive selects loss of fixed position
words.prose: {{ar:تَزُولَ}} ({{tr:tazūla}}) names departure from fixed position, not passive removal. Its Form I intransitive frame makes the mountains the departing subject, while the governing lām keeps the movement dependent; variant readings expose whether that departure is subordinated, asserted, or caught between the two. The root also answers 14:44 and contrasts with mountain-travel formulas at 52:10 and 78:20. The softer z-l motion of the verb before the heavier final noun remains secondary, but it lets the sound carry slipping movement into the closing mountain mass.

topics.headline: dependent mood with assertion variants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb is the mood pressure point: dependent in the main surface, stronger in indicative/emphatic variants, and therefore central to the clause's scale.
topics.reason: The canonical form is subjunctive under lām; accepted variant evidence is retained to mark the interpretive tension without overriding the local mood.

topics.headline: mountains depart as collective subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mountains are not objects being removed; grammar makes the whole mountain class the subject that would leave its place.
topics.reason: The verb is Form I intransitive, feminine singular for a non-rational plural subject, with al-jibāl as fāʿil.

topics.headline: z-w-l as loss of fixity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the image is not generic vanishing but the tipping or departure of what should remain fixed.
topics.reason: The minhu complement and z-w-l semantic range support departure from an anchored position.

topics.headline: rare mountain-displacement scale
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 14:46 measures the plot against cosmic stability: z-w-l loss of position answers 14:44 and differs from mountain travel at 52:10 and 78:20.
topics.reason: The rows support a rare z-w-l plus mountain pairing and concrete inter-ayah contrasts, while the local conditional frame controls the hyperbole.

topics.headline: sliding sound before mountain mass
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a sound texture that suits motion before the heavier final noun, though it remains secondary to grammar and semantics.
topics.reason: The phonetic row is coherent but functions as local stylistic support rather than a separate semantic branch.

words.gloss_range: source/cause preposition plus pronoun, mediating between departure verb and final mountain subject
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْهُ}} ({{tr:minhu}}) supplies the source or cause complement before the mountains arrive. The pronoun is compressed and backward-looking: it can route to the plot, and less directly to God's domain, while a variant that expands it toward their plot confirms that the compact pronoun is an interpretive pressure point. The local departure verb blocks a weak partitive reading, so the phrase means from it, from him, or because of it rather than some of it.

topics.headline: source/cause complement before subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the source or cause relation is heard before the final subject, so the mountain image arrives already mediated.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence ties the prepositional phrase to tazūla as its governed complement.

topics.headline: compressed backward pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the suffix must be routed backward through the dense field of plot and God, changing whether source, cause, or domain is foregrounded.
topics.reason: The rows preserve live antecedent pressure while keeping the preposition attached to the departure verb.

topics.headline: not partitive; variant names plot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local limit: min is not weakly partitive here, and the expanded variant makes the plot-source reading explicit.
topics.reason: The intransitive departure frame selects source/cause, and the variant is retained as support for the standard pronoun's compactness.

words.gloss_range: definite plural mountains as collective subject and final benchmark of immovable stability
words.root_gloss_range: mountain/fixed-formation root range; local noun is the definite plural class of mountains as the benchmark of created stability
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْجِبَالُ}} ({{tr:al-jibālu}}) lands as the final mass of the ayah. It is definite, plural, and nominative as the subject of the intransitive verb, so the plot is measured against the recognizable class of mountains as created fixity itself; the closing image turns the stability formulas of 16:15, 21:31, and 78:7 into a conditional test of displacement, while 14:44 supplies the nearby removal-denial pressure.

topics.headline: known mountain class as subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final noun is not some mountain or a passive object; it is the definite mountain class acting as the grammatical subject of departure.
topics.reason: The noun is definite plural, nominative fāʿil of the intransitive verb, with non-rational plural agreement.

topics.headline: mountains as created fixity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the benchmark is not bare rock but the visible emblem of formed, innate stability being imagined as losing place.
topics.reason: Root-family evidence supports mountain and innate-formation pressure, while local syntax keeps the noun concrete and imagistic.

topics.headline: stabilizers turned into displacement test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 14:46 joins a cosmic-disruption field while contrasting stabilizing mountain formulas at 16:15, 21:31, and 78:7, and it intensifies the same-surah removal issue from 14:44.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah and rarity rows are retained as marked contextual pressure, but the local z-w-l plus j-b-l grammar remains decisive.

topics.headline: heaviest final landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes by converting abstract scheming into the heaviest possible image: stability itself becoming unstable.
topics.reason: The final-position, sound, and synthesis rows converge with the grammar of the noun as subject of departure.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated مكر and the construction لتزول منه الجبال.
baseline_models.mechanism: The scheme is measured against a displacement threshold: زوال supplies departure from place or state, while جبال supplies elevated solidity. The clause therefore scales the plot by its intended capacity to dislodge what ordinarily defines stability.

activation_trace.role: Departure from a place or condition supplies the plot's targeted effect.
An elevated solid mass supplies the limiting object against which the plot is scaled.

changed_reading.before: They executed an exceptionally great plot.
changed_reading.after: Their plot is represented as a displacement force aimed at what most visibly embodies fixedness.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وعند الله مكرهم, placed between the repeated possessive phrases مكرهم.
baseline_models.mechanism: The plot is grammatically theirs yet also present at the divine locus. Proximity and presence make human possession non-exclusive: the scheme never leaves the field of divine knowledge, judgment, or disposal.

activation_trace.role: Nearness and presence turn عند الله into the plot's second, overriding relation.

changed_reading.after: Their plot is fully present before God, so their authorship does not amount to sovereign custody or control.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The plural الجبال as the object of removal.
baseline_models.mechanism: The mountain image can carry great collectivities and leading figures as well as terrain. Joined to مزاولة as handling or contest, the plot can target a social order by working on its masses and chiefs until their positions shift.

activation_trace.role: Mountain-like multitude opens a collective rather than solely geological object.
Chiefs likened to mountains supply the elevated nodes of the social structure.
Handling and contesting supply a process by which entrenched people or leaders are made to shift.

changed_reading.before: The mountains are a hyperbolic image of physical magnitude.
changed_reading.after: The mountains may also be entrenched collectivities and chiefs that the scheme works to reposition.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah first stages a coercive attempt to drive messengers out of the land, then reverses it by settling them there, and later points to habitation in the wrongdoers' former dwellings. Mountain-removing plot thus becomes a contest over who can displace whom and whose settlement endures.

activation_trace.role: Mountain-like collectivity lets displacement operate on peoples as well as terrain.
Penetration to the outside gives the antagonists' threat its concrete expulsive vector.
Settlement in a dwelling supplies the divinely promised reversal of expulsion.
Inhabiting the former wrongdoers' dwellings makes reversed occupancy an observed historical pattern.

structural_cues: 14:13 threatens expulsion or forced return; 14:14 answers with destruction and resettlement.
14:45 immediately recalls living in the dwellings of earlier wrongdoers before 14:46 names the plot.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies expulsion, counter-settlement, and inherited dwellings; I map these spatial reversals onto the mountain-removal predicate. The live alternative is that the mountains remain only a magnitude comparison.

changed_reading.before: The plot is great enough to move mountains.
changed_reading.after: The plot is the coercive architecture of expulsion and forced return, but the surah reverses its claimed power by transferring settlement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The mountain clause states the scale of the plot's projected effect, while 14:18 renders the wrongdoers' works as burnt residue scattered by violent wind and beyond their power to retain. The context separates intended reach from durable achievement.

activation_trace.role: Solid elevation supplies the plot's maximal projected object.
Ash from burning supplies the achieved works' loss of cohesion.
Blowing air supplies the carrier that removes the disintegrated works.
A violent wind that makes things light and scatters them supplies the destructive transport.
Capacity that reaches action or possession is explicitly denied over what they acquired.

structural_cues: 14:18 juxtaposes accumulated works with ash, storm wind, and inability to retain any result.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mountain-scale intended movement and ash-like unretainable works; I distinguish projected efficacy from lasting yield. A live alternative is that the plot did cause large temporal disruptions even though its final yield vanished.

changed_reading.before: The plot's mountain-moving scale directly indicates its successful power.
changed_reading.after: Its intended reach may be mountain-sized while its retained result is ash-sized.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exposed hierarchy of proud leaders and followers is followed by Satan's denial of coercive authority: he called and they answered. With mountains carrying chiefs and multitudes, the plot works as distributed social movement through prestige, allegiance, and invitation rather than irresistible force.

activation_trace.role: Chiefs figured as mountains provide the high points of the hierarchy.
Mountain-like multitudes provide the social mass that follows those high points.
Elevated rank and leadership identify the socially mountainous actors.
Allegiance and succession supply the linkage through which a hierarchy moves.
Capacity and governing authority are denied, limiting the mechanism's coercive component.
Calling and inclining by speech supplies the non-coercive transmission mechanism.

structural_cues: 14:21 exposes followers and self-exalting leaders together.
14:22 replaces coercive authority with a call that received a response and returns blame to the respondents.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hierarchy, allegiance, denied authority, and answered invitation; I infer that social mountains move through coordinated consent and prestige. The alternative is a broader political plot using both persuasion and coercion.

changed_reading.before: A centralized plot applies overwhelming force to fixed objects.
changed_reading.after: A plot can move social mountains by propagating invitation through leaders, followers, and their own responses.

context_deltas.mechanism: The good word is a rooted tree whose origin remains fixed; the bad word is pulled out whole and has no stable base; God then stabilizes believers by the fixed word. Mountains become the surah's maximal image for rooted semantic and communal order, and the plot becomes an anti-rooting operation.

activation_trace.role: A created, impressed disposition lets the mountain image carry durable formed order.
Continuance and fixedness supply the good word's rooted resistance.
Pulling a thing wholly from its root supplies the precise counter-operation to stability.
Stability and settledness name what the uprooted bad word lacks.
Active strengthening turns fixedness into divine resistance rather than static inertia.

structural_cues: 14:24-27 forms a continuous fixed-root, total-uprooting, no-settlement, divine-stabilization sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opposed rooting and uprooting processes; I map the mountain onto their strongest image of formed stability and the plot onto the uprooting side. The literal mountain comparison remains live.

changed_reading.before: The plot threatens massive physical structures.
changed_reading.after: The plot threatens the rooted word and the stable human order it forms, while divine تثبيت supplies the counterforce.

context_deltas.mechanism: A remote مكر branch means watering hard land before plowing. The surah's rain-to-fruit sequence and its uncultivated valley activate that branch as a material analogy: the plot is preparatory saturation meant to make resistant ground workable, but it counterfeits the divine cultivation that produces provision.

activation_trace.role: Watering hard ground before tillage supplies a covert preparatory operation for the plot.
Ground too solid to excavate supplies the resistant substrate the preparation seeks to overcome.
Delivered water supplies the surah's explicit productive irrigation process.
Ripe fruit supplies the beneficial yield of divine watering.
Cultivation and growth, explicitly absent from the valley, sharpen the problem of making hard land productive.

strongest_changes: The 14:44/14:46 زوال repetition exposes a double standard: permanence claimed for the plotters and removal directed at stable orders.

summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly opposed movement to settlement and rootedness, then supplied an immediate reversed زوال echo. It also made the remote soil-watering branch of مكر mechanically coherent against the rain, fruit, barren valley, and unexcavable-ground images.

Literal mountains, chiefs and collectivities, and rooted word-order can coexist, but their relative priority remains open.
The cultivation, coating, and internal-spoilage mechanisms are branch-triggered analogies rather than replacements for the ordinary lexical reading of مكر.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Plotting is bounded by presence even at mountain-moving scale.** The packet's accepted `م ك ر` inventory lacks the ordinary plotting branch; the fixed repeated construction itself supplies deliberate scheme, while `ع ن د` `B004` gives presence/proximity, `ز و ل` `B001` departure from state, and `ج ب ل` `B001` high solid mass plus `B009` difficulty/prevention. I do not import an unattested `م ك ر` branch. Structurally, their scheme is repeated but then located “with God”; I infer this location encloses its reach. The ayah reads as maximal destabilizing capacity already held within a superior field of knowledge.

2. **Mountains can stand for formed resistance as well as matter.** `ج ب ل` `B004` is innate formed nature and `B012` chiefs like mountains; `ز و ل` `B001` permits removal from state. Earlier arrogant leaders route whole peoples into ruin. I infer a plot may seek to dislodge entrenched orders or towering authorities, not only physical mountains. This reading remains exploratory because the grammar favors the hyperbolic material image.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayah 14:47 supplied the correction the plot image needs: destabilizing power may move what appears firm, but it cannot make the promised outcome fail to arrive.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The schemes are fully present within divine custody.** `ع ن د B004` supplies proximity and presence at something. The repeated `مَكْر` is placed `عِندَ ٱللَّه`; 14:42 denied heedlessness, 14:45 supplied clarity through examples, and 14:47 denies promise-failure. The packet supplies presence inside that knowledge-account sequence; I infer custody rather than spatial nearness alone. `وَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَكْرُهُمْ` reads as no scheme having an outside from which to evade reckoning.
2. **Human destabilization is measured against solid mass and divine transformation.** `ز و ل B001/B002` supplies departure and movement, while `ج ب ل B001` supplies a high solid mass and `ج ب ل B005` hardness that stops digging. The schemes are scaled to mountain movement; 14:44 had quoted a claim of no departure, and 14:48 actually transforms earth and heavens. The packet supplies attempted movement versus effected transformation; I infer a contrast between human reach and divine world-remapping. Mountains serve as the resistance measure of the scheme.

No `م ك ر` branch is retained as an activated lexical reading: its accepted packet inventory contains calf-build, plant, pigment, irrigation, and spoiled-date branches, and this eleven-ayah window supplies no visible mechanism strong enough to attach any of them to the fixed forms. The repetition remains a structural cue, but forcing an inventory branch would hide the abductive gap.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 14:48 supplied the crucial correction: human schemes are only measured against moving solid masses, whereas divine action actually remaps earth and sky. 14:51's accounting then confirmed that “with God” assigns custody and eventual processing.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, ana çizgide sınırı aşma, doğru olduğu bilinen şeyi geri çevirme ve ona karşı koymayı birlikte verir. Bununla birlikte birine karşı aynı işi yaparak boy ölçüşme ve devenin yuları tutana üstün gelmesi de tanıklanır; bu kullanımların tümünü yalnızca doğruyu reddetme diye açıklamak kapsamı gereksiz yere daraltır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Ana anlam bilinçli karşı koyma ve ölçüyü aşmadır; yarışma ve yulara üstün gelme bunun özel, doğruyu reddetmeye bağlı olmayan gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Kişi ölçüyü aşar, doğruyu bildiği halde onu kabul etmez ve karşı koyar.

Deve, yulara yüklenip onu tutan kişiye üstün gelerek onu çekebilir.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlığa tapınma eylemini ve kişinin kendini tapınmaya vermesini anlatır. Türemiş kullanımlarda bir varlığı tapınılır kılmayı, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınma konusu sayılan varlıkları da adlandırır.

facets.statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
Ettirgen kullanım, bir varlığı başkalarınca tapınılır duruma getirme veya öyle sunma işlemini bildirir.
Güneşe kimi topluluklarca tapınılması nedeniyle ona tapınılan varlık anlamındaki bir ad verilmesi, varlık anlamının tarihsel bir örneğidir.

Özel adın doğrudan ya da seslenme öğesi yerine geçen bir sonla kullanılması, yakarma ve dilek bildiren seslenme biçimleri kurar.
Ses veya parçaların düşürüldüğü kısalmış biçimler, şaşma ve ant anlatan kalıplarda kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Bu dal, kanıtta tek üretken kök çekirdeğine indirgenmeyen sınırlı adlandırma malzemesini taşır. Yapısal bölme şartı koşmadan, yalnız verilen biçim ve bağlam sınırı içinde kontrollü adlandırma kümesi olarak tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kayıt genel kök anlamı gibi genişletilmemeli, içindeki öğeler birbirinin yerine geçen tek bir sözlük karşılığı sayılmamalı ve yalnız kanıtın verdiği adlandırma sınırı içinde kullanılmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kapsam verilen biçim, adlandırma veya özel kullanım sınırıyla bağlıdır; ortak bir yalın anlam ya da üretken genel kullanım varsayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bu küme tek bir kavram değildir: yaygın kişi nitelemesi çevik, zarif ya da becerikli kişiyi anlatırken aynı ses biçimi şahin, erkeklik organı, yiğit kişi ve cömert kişi için de ayrı ad olarak verilmiştir.

facets.statement: İnsan için kullanılan ana niteleme çeviklik, zariflik ve beceriklilik özelliklerini birleştirir.
Kadın için gözü açık, iş bitirici ya da toplum içinde görünür olma nitelikleri ayrıca verilir.
Şahin ve erkeklik organı aynı biçimin kişi nitelemesiyle kavramsal bağ kurmayan ayrı adlandırmalarıdır.
Yiğit ve cömert kişi anlamları da ana çeviklik ve zariflik nitelemesinden ayrı değerlendirilmelidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt, tek bir birleşik anlamdan çok sınırlı veya biçime bağlı adlandırmaları gösterir; dal bu kayıtları kontrollü biçimde görünür tutar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tekilde topluluğun önderi ve bilgini, çoğul yapıda ise topluluğun ileri gelenleri anlamını doğrudan verir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal kalabalık halkı veya doğal dağları değil, topluluk içinde öne çıkan önder ve bilgin kişileri belirtir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın biçim tek bir önder veya bilgini, bağlı çoğul yapı ise belirli bir topluluğun ileri gelenlerini bildirir.

concept_map.definition: Bir topluluğun önderi ve bilgini olan seçkin kişiyi belirtir; çoğul yapıda o topluluğun ileri gelenlerini topluca adlandırır.

facets.statement: Topluluk içinde önderlik ve bilgi bakımından öne çıkan kişiyi belirtir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tek tanıklık, önder ve bilgin kişiyi tekil olarak; bir topluluğun ileri gelenlerini ise çoğul yapı içinde verir.
